## a) (2 pts) Use the lm( ) function in R to obtain the estimated regression function.
```{r a, include=TRUE}
lm1 <- lm(minutes ~ machines, data1)
summary(lm1)
```

## b) (3 pts) Using R as a calculator, obtain SSTO.
```{r b, include=TRUE}
# SSTO = summation((y(i) - y(hat))^2)
b1 = 14.7383
b0 = -2.3221
yhat <- b0 + b1*(data1$machines)
e <- (data1$minutes)-yhat
yi <- b0 + (b1*(data1$machines)) + e
cbind(e, yi)
SSTO <- (yi - yhat)^2
SSTO <- sum(SSTO)
SSTO
```

## c) (3 pts) Using R as a calculator, obtain SSR. You can use the fitted values from the regression in (a).
```{r c, include=TRUE}
# SSR = sum((yhat - ybar)^2)
ybar <- mean(data1$minutes)
SSR <- (yhat - ybar)^2
SSR <- sum(SSR)
SSR
```
## d) (3 pts) Using R as a calculator, obtain SSE. You can use the fitted values from the regression in (a).
```{r d, include=TRUE}
# SSE = sum((yi - yhat)^2)
SSE <- (yi - yhat)^2
SSE <- sum(SSE)
SSE
```
## e) (6 pts) Using the pieces above, manually construct the complete ANOVA table for the regression analysis, with columns for Source of variation, SS, df, and MS.
```{r e, include=TRUE}
n <- length(data1$minutes)
MSE <- SSE/(n-2)
MSE
MSR <- SSR/1
MSR
EMSE <- var(data1$minutes)
EMSE
EMSR <- (data1$machines - mean(data1$machines))^2
EMSR <- sum(EMSR)
EMSR <- (b1^2)*EMSR
EMSR <- var(data1$machines) + EMSR
EMSR
```
## f) (2 pts) Obtain the same ANOVA table using R.
```{r f, include=TRUE}
anova_model <- aov(minutes ~ machines, data = data1)
summary(anova_model)
```

## i) (5 pts) In R, plot the deviations (Yi – Yi(hat)) against Xi on a graph. Plot the deviations (Yi(hat) – Ybar) against Xi on another graph, using the same scales as for the first graph. From your two graphs, does SSE or SSR appear to be the larger component of SSTO?
```{r i, include=TRUE}
# Deviations
SSR_dev <- (yhat - ybar)
SSE_dev <- (yi - yhat)

# Common y-axis scale for both plots
ylim_common <- range(c(SSE_dev,SSR_dev))

# Plot deviations associated with SSE
plot(data1$machines, SSE_dev,
     xlab = "Machines",
     ylab = "Deviations on SSE",
     main = "Residual Deviations",
     ylim = ylim_common,
     pch = 19)

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)


# Plot deviations associated with SSR
plot(data1$machines, SSR_dev,
     xlab = "Machines",
     ylab = "Deviations on SSR",
     main = "Regression Deviations",
     ylim = ylim_common,
     pch = 19)

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```
